title: Count Prefix and Suffix Pairs I
spaceBreakdown:
- no containers allocated; only a few int/bool locals
- recursion depth: none
- not counted: input vector, returned int
approach: The constraints are tiny (n ≤ 50, each word ≤ 10 chars), so a direct enumeration of all index pairs (i,j) with i<j is optimal. For each pair, check that words[i] is no longer than words[j], that the first |words[i]| characters of words[j] equal words[i], and that the last |words[i]| characters of words[j] also equal words[i]. Count every pair that satisfies both conditions.
hints: With n ≤ 50 and each word at most 10 characters, how many index pairs (i,j) with i<j exist, and is that number small enough to test each one directly?

Enumerate every pair (i,j) with i<j and, for each, verify words[i] equals both the first |words[i]| characters and the last |words[i]| characters of words[j]. Example: words[1]="aba" vs words[2]="ababa" - first 3 chars "aba" and last 3 chars "aba" both match, so count it.

**Single element** - only one word, so no pairs exist
`Input: words = ["a"]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: starting the inner loop at j=i instead of j=i+1 → counts (0,0) as a valid pair → returns 1

**str1 longer than str2** - the length guard must come first
`Input: words = ["abab","ab"]` → `Expected: 0`
⚠️ Bug: comparing characters without checking |str1| <= |str2| first → reads out of bounds or miscompares → returns 1

**All equal words** - every ordered pair with i<j counts
`Input: words = ["a","a","a"]` → `Expected: 3`
⚠️ Bug: skipping pairs where the two strings are equal → returns 0

**Single-character words** - prefix and suffix are the same single char
`Input: words = ["a","a"]` → `Expected: 1`
⚠️ Bug: requiring the prefix and suffix regions to be disjoint/non-overlapping → returns 0

followUps.q: If words.length grows to 10^5 but each word is still ≤ 10 characters, how would you keep it fast?
followUps.a: For each word j, enumerate every length L from 1 to 10 and form the prefix of length L; if it also equals the suffix of length L, hash it and add the count of earlier words equal to that string. Time O(n·L), space O(n·L).

followUps.q: If each word can be up to 10^5 characters long, how do you avoid O(L) per comparison?
followUps.a: Precompute the Z-array (or rolling hash) of each word to find, in O(L), all lengths L such that the prefix of length L is also a suffix, then look up earlier words by those prefixes in a hash map. Time O(total characters), space O(total characters).

followUps.q: If words arrive in a stream and you must report the running count after each arrival, what changes?
followUps.a: Maintain a hash map from string to frequency of all words seen so far; on each new word, enumerate its valid prefix-also-suffix lengths, sum the frequencies of those exact strings, append the answer, then insert the new word into the map. Time O(L) per arrival, space O(total characters seen).
